nvme get-feature /dev/nvme0 -n 1 -f 0x84; nvme id-ns -H NSATTR; blockdev --getro.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c namespace update path sets the disk read-only from NSATTR (NVME_NS_ATTR_RO). The status itself → -EIO.
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: nvme set-feature /dev/nvme0 -n 1 -f 0x84 -v 1 (Write Protect, reversible), write, then set it back to 0. Never use the permanent value on a drive you want to keep.
S-21Command Interrupted (SCT 0 / SC 0x21) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: CQE 0x21 → host waits the CRD time → same command re-submitted.
What happens
The controller stopped processing the command (internal event, ANA-related change, resource rebalance) and asks the host to retry, often with a Command Retry Delay.
How it shows up
SC 0x21 with DNR=0 by definition. If the retries run out, Linux maps it to BLK_STS_TARGET → -EREMOTEIO ("critical target error").
Spec basis
Generic "Command Interrupted": "the host should retry the command" (libnvme). CRD field + CRDT1–3 + ACRE.
Typical causes
Firmware busy with a background operation; controller-level events in dual-port arrays; QEMU returns it as an internal status for interrupted zone/atomic operations (defined as NVME_COMMAND_INTERRUPTED).
How to detect / prove
Trace with nvme:nvme_complete_rq (status 0x21 with retries > 0) and command_retries_count. Check CRD values against nvme id-ctrl crdt1..3.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() → BLK_STS_TARGET; nvme_retry_req() CRD delay; nvme_configure_host_options() ACRE.
Test to provoke it
SAFE: fault-inject status 0x21 with dont_retry=0 (§3.5) to see the retry and errno behaviour.
S-22Transient Transport Error (SCT 0 / SC 0x22) ReportedNVMe-oF transport
In a PEX trace
Not visible Not on PCIe at all: NVMe-oF statuses travel in TCP/RDMA/FC response capsules, so a PEX capture of the NIC/HBA link shows only encrypted or opaque network DMA. Use a network capture (Wireshark NVMe/TCP dissector) or target logs. Pattern: On the network capture: retransmissions or digest mismatches just before the response capsule.
What happens
A short-lived transport problem made the command fail. Retrying on the same controller should work. libnvme quotes the spec: after four or more failures with this status, treat it as a persistent transport error.
How it shows up
SC 0x22, DNR=0. Linux retries (up to 5) and then gives -EIO. It is not in SCT 3, so Linux multipath does not fail over on it directly.
Spec basis
Generic "Transient Transport Error"; transport bindings (TCP, RDMA, FC).
Typical causes
Packet loss or digest errors (NVMe/TCP HDGST/DDGST), RDMA retry exhaustion, FC link resets.
How to detect / prove
Network counters (ethtool -S, RDMA counters), NVMe/TCP digest error messages in dmesg; correlation with retries in the tracepoint.
Linux v7.2 source
Default retry/COMPLETE path in core.c; transport drivers in tcp.c/rdma.c.
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: NVMe/TCP with tc netem corrupt plus data digest enabled.
S-23Admin Command Media Not Ready (SCT 0 / SC 0x24) ReportedNVMe admin
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: CC write with CRIME=1 → CSTS.RDY=1 quickly → admin command → CQE 0x24.
What happens
The admin command needs the media, but the media is not ready yet. This can happen when the controller became ready early (CSTS.RDY) because the host set CC.CRIME (Controller Ready Independent of Media Enable).
How it shows up
SC 0x24 on admin commands such as Identify Namespace, Get Log Page of media-backed logs, Format.
Spec basis
CAP.CRMS (CRWMS/CRIMS), CC.CRIME, CRTO register (Controller Ready Timeouts).
Typical causes
Host using CRIME mode and sending media-dependent commands before media ready; large drives whose internal metadata load takes seconds.
How to detect / prove
Check CC.CRIME in a register dump or trace; compare time since CC.EN with CRTO.CRIMT.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_enable_ctrl() clears CRIME on purpose: "Setting CRIME results in CSTS.RDY before the media is ready. This makes it possible for media related commands to return the error NVME_SC_ADMIN_COMMAND_MEDIA_NOT_READY. Until the driver is restructured to handle retries, disable CC.CRIME." So Linux should never see this code.
Test to provoke it
EXPERT: user-space driver enabling with CRIME=1 on a CAP.CRMS-capable drive and sending Identify NS at once.
S-24I/O Command Set errors: Invalid I/O Command Set (0x2C) and the 0x29–0x2B group ReportedNVMe admin
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Identify with CNS 05h/06h and a CSI value → immediate CQE.
What happens
A command references a Command Set Identifier (CSI) that the controller does not support, has not enabled, or cannot combine with the others.
How it shows up
Linux defines NVME_SC_INVALID_IO_CMD_SET = 0x2C in the Generic range. QEMU (NVME_INVALID_IOCS = 0x012c) and libnvme (NVME_SC_INVALID_IOCS = 0x2c under "Command Set Specific – Namespace Types") place it in SCT 1, along with 0x29 I/O Command Set Not Supported, 0x2A Not Enabled, 0x2B Combination Rejected. uncertain Verify the SCT in the spec. A Linux string lookup of a real SCT 1 / 0x2C status prints "Unknown" because 0x12C has no entry.
Spec basis
I/O Command Set Profile feature (FID 19h), Identify I/O Command Set data structure (CNS 1Ch), CC.CSS.
Typical causes
QEMU: nvme_identify_ns() returns INVALID_IOCS for a namespace whose CSI is not enabled; nvme_set_feature() returns IOCS_NOT_SUPPORTED / COMBINATION_REJECTED. Real: tools asking for ZNS/KV identify data on an NVM-only controller.
How to detect / prove
nvme id-iocs /dev/nvme0; nvme get-feature -f 0x19.
Linux v7.2 source
Linux sets CC.CSS to NVME_CC_CSS_CSI when CAP.CSS allows it (core.c:nvme_enable_ctrl()) and ignores namespaces with unsupported CSI during scan.
Test to provoke it
SAFE: nvme admin-passthru /dev/nvme0 --opcode=0x06 --cdw10=0x05 --cdw11=0x05000000 -r -l 4096 --namespace-id=1 (Identify CNS 05h with an unsupported CSI value).
S-25LBA Out of Range (SCT 0 / SC 0x80) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: SQE with SLBA near the end of the namespace → immediate CQE.
What happens
SLBA + NLB goes past the namespace size (NSZE), or the arithmetic overflows. Nothing is transferred.
How it shows up
SC 0x80, DNR=1 in QEMU. Linux maps it to BLK_STS_TARGET → -EREMOTEIO ("critical target error"), not EIO, which surprises people searching logs.
Spec basis
Generic (I/O command set) "LBA Out of Range"; Identify Namespace NSZE.
Typical causes
Namespace shrunk/recreated while the host kept the old size (no rescan); partition table from a larger drive copied to a smaller one; block-layer sector-to-LBA conversion bugs with mixed 512/4096 formats. QEMU: nvme_check_bounds(): if (UINT64_MAX - slba < nlb || slba + nlb > nsze).
How to detect / prove
dmesg error line shows "@ LBA x, n blocks". Compare with nvme id-ns NSZE and blockdev --getsize64. A mismatch means a stale capacity.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() (BLK_STS_TARGET); capacity updates in nvme_update_ns_info() after rescans.
Test to provoke it
SAFE: nvme read /dev/nvme0n1 -s <NSZE> -c 0 -z 4096 (read the block just past the end).
S-26Capacity Exceeded (SCT 0 / SC 0x81) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Write SQE → CQE 0x81, possibly after data transfer.
What happens
Running the command would make the namespace use more than its capacity (NCAP). This only matters for thin-provisioned namespaces, where NCAP < NSZE.
How it shows up
SC 0x81. Linux maps it to BLK_STS_NOSPC → -ENOSPC: the filesystem gets "no space" even though df shows free space.
Spec basis
Identify Namespace NSZE, NCAP, NUSE; thin provisioning (NSFEAT bit 0).
Typical causes
Over-subscribed thin namespace; host not sending Deallocate (discard), so NUSE never shrinks; deallocations the drive accepts but does not apply (see silent-failure part).
How to detect / prove
Watch NUSE vs NCAP with nvme id-ns over time; compare with filesystem usage. If NUSE stays high after fstrim, deallocation is not taking effect.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() → BLK_STS_NOSPC.
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: thin namespace (QEMU or array) filled past NCAP with fio.
S-27Namespace Not Ready (SCT 0 / SC 0x82) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Immediate CQE 0x82 to I/O shortly after controller enable.
What happens
The namespace cannot be accessed right now, for a reason other than an ANA state (libnvme wording). Examples: still coming up after reset, a background operation, or a namespace that is being created.
How it shows up
SC 0x82. DNR=0 means "try again later", DNR=1 means "will not become ready". Linux → BLK_STS_TARGET → -EREMOTEIO once retries are used up.
Spec basis
Generic "Namespace Not Ready"; Identify Namespace / I/O Command Set Independent NS data "Namespace Ready" indications in newer revisions (verify in spec).
Typical causes
Command sent right after reset or namespace attach on a drive that rebuilds mapping tables; a drive in a vendor "failure" mode returning 0x82 to everything.
How to detect / prove
Time since CSTS.RDY; check whether it clears by itself (poll with nvme read each second). Persistent 0x82 with DNR=1 is a dead namespace.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() → BLK_STS_TARGET.
Test to provoke it
SAFE via fault injection (status 0x082).
S-28Reservation Conflict (SCT 0 / SC 0x83) ReportedNVMe command / reservations
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: I/O SQE → immediate CQE 0x83.
What happens
Another host holds a reservation on the namespace that does not allow this host's access (for example, Write Exclusive held by another host, and this host writes).
How it shows up
SC 0x83, normally DNR=1. Linux maps it to BLK_STS_RESV_CONFLICT → -EBADE; the persistent-reservation API returns PR_STS_RESERVATION_CONFLICT.
Spec basis
Reservation types (Write Exclusive, Exclusive Access, Registrants Only, All Registrants); Reservation Report.
Typical causes
Cluster software fenced this node; stale reservation left by a crashed node; a host that has not registered its key after reboot.
How to detect / prove
nvme resv-report /dev/nvme0n1 -c 1 shows holder, type and registrants; compare with this host's Host ID (nvme get-feature -f 0x81).
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status(); pr.c:nvme_status_to_pr_err().
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: nvme resv-register + resv-acquire -t 1 (Write Exclusive) from controller A, write from controller B.
S-29Format In Progress (SCT 0 / SC 0x84) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Format SQE without its CQE yet; I/O CQEs with 0x84.
What happens
A Format NVM is running on the namespace; I/O to it is rejected until it completes.
How it shows up
SC 0x84 on I/O, DNR typically 0. Linux retries a few times, then -EIO.
Spec basis
Format NVM (80h); Identify Controller FNA (Format NVM Attributes, e.g. whether a format applies to all namespaces). Some drives report progress in a vendor log.
Typical causes
Format issued by another tool or host on a shared namespace, or on a "format all namespaces" drive (FNA bit) where formatting one namespace blocks the others. QEMU: nvme_do_format() sets ns->status = NVME_FORMAT_IN_PROGRESS and I/O to that namespace returns it until done.
How to detect / prove
Look for an earlier Format SQE (opcode 80h) in the trace or in the admin nvme_setup_cmd tracepoint; Persistent Event log Format NVM Start/Completion events (07h/08h).
Linux v7.2 source
Default handling; the kernel itself never formats.
Test to provoke it
DESTRUCTIVE / CAUTION: on a scratch namespace in QEMU, nvme format /dev/nvme0n1 -s 1 (user-data erase; slower) and read from another shell.
💡 Senior insight

When a new drive fails qualification with "-EOPNOTSUPP" or "-EREMOTEIO" in an application, translate back with the table in §3.4.2 before blaming the application. EREMOTEIO always means LBA Out of Range, Namespace Not Ready or Command Interrupted. Those three have very different root causes, and the dmesg nvme_log_error line (if it printed) tells you which one. If it did not print, the request was RQF_QUIET or the error came from somewhere other than the NVMe driver.

5 Command Specific Status (SCT 1)

← 4 Generic Command Status (SCT 0)6 Media and Data Integrity (SCT 2) and Path Related (SCT 3) →

SCT 1 codes only make sense together with the opcode that got them. SC 0x00–0x7F are defined per admin command (queue management, firmware, namespace management, virtualization). SC 0x80–0xBF are defined per I/O command set: for the NVM command set (0x80–0x8x), for Fabrics commands (the same numbers, different meanings), and for Zoned Namespaces (0xB6–0xBF). In Linux's shifted layout they are 0x100–0x1FF. Always decode an SCT 1 status with the opcode next to it. 0x180 is "Conflicting Attributes" for a Dataset Management command but "Incompatible Format" for a Fabrics Connect.

💡 Linux ignores some of these on purpose

drivers/nvme/host/pci.c:nvme_create_io_queues() says: "Ignore failing Create SQ/CQ commands, we can continue with less than the desired amount of queues, and even a controller without I/O queues can still be used to issue admin commands." A drive that rejects queue creation with an SCT 1 code (0x100–0x102, 0x108) therefore does not fail probe. The result is a working but slower device with fewer queues. The error is reported, but in practice it shows up as a performance anomaly. Check ls /sys/block/nvme0n1/mq | wc -l against the CPU count.

S-30Completion Queue Invalid (SCT 1 / SC 0x00) ReportedNVMe admin / queues
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Create SQ with CQID=n where no earlier successful Create CQ n exists.
What happens
Create I/O SQ named a CQID that does not exist (or is 0), or Delete I/O CQ named an invalid CQ.
How it shows up
Linux 0x100 "Completion Queue Invalid" on the admin command; queue setup continues with fewer queues (see callout above).
Spec basis
Create I/O Submission Queue (01h) CDW11 CQID; Delete I/O Completion Queue (04h).
Typical causes
Host creating the SQ before its CQ, or after a failed CQ creation; QEMU nvme_create_sq() and nvme_del_cq(): if (!cqid || nvme_check_cqid(n, cqid)) return NVME_INVALID_CQID | NVME_DNR.
How to detect / prove
Admin command order in the trace: Create CQ (05h) must complete successfully before Create SQ (01h) uses its ID.
Linux v7.2 source
pci.c:nvme_create_queue() → adapter_alloc_cq() then adapter_alloc_sq().
Test to provoke it
EXPERT: user-space driver creating SQ 1 bound to CQ 7 that was never created.
S-31Invalid Queue Identifier (SCT 1 / SC 0x01) ReportedNVMe admin / queues
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Set Features FID 07h CQE DW0 = e.g. 0x00070007 (8 SQ + 8 CQ), then Create CQ with QID 9.
What happens
Create I/O SQ/CQ used a QID that is 0, already in use, or above the number of queues granted by Set Features Number of Queues. Also used by Delete I/O SQ for a bad SQID.
How it shows up
Linux 0x101; queue creation stops at that queue.
Spec basis
Number of Queues feature (FID 07h) result NSQA/NCQA (0's based); Create/Delete queue commands.
Typical causes
Host asked for N queues, got fewer in the Set Features result, and created N anyway; QID reuse without deleting. QEMU: nvme_create_sq()/nvme_create_cq() check qid > n->conf_ioqpairs || n->sq[qid] != NULL.
How to detect / prove
Decode the Number of Queues completion Dword 0 in the trace and compare with the highest QID created.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_set_queue_count() uses the granted count. pci.c:nvme_setup_io_queues() sizes the queues from it.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: start with -device nvme,max_ioqpairs=4 and create queue 5 from a user-space driver.
S-32Invalid Queue Size (SCT 1 / SC 0x02) ReportedNVMe admin / queues
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Create CQ CDW10 = (QSIZE<<16)|QID with QSIZE > MQES.
What happens
The queue size in Create I/O SQ/CQ is 0 or bigger than CAP.MQES+1, or (QEMU) the CC.IOSQES/IOCQES entry sizes are not 64/16 bytes.
How it shows up
Linux 0x102 "Invalid Queue Size".
Spec basis
CAP.MQES (0's based maximum queue entries); CAP.CQR (contiguous queues required); CC.IOSQES/IOCQES.
Typical causes
Host ignoring MQES; a device that reports MQES wrongly (Linux has quirks for this). QEMU: nvme_create_cq()/nvme_create_sq() return NVME_MAX_QSIZE_EXCEEDED | NVME_DNR.
How to detect / prove
Read CAP (nvme show-regs /dev/nvme0 -H) and the QSIZE field (CDW10 bits 31:16) of the Create command.
Linux v7.2 source
pci.c: queue depth is limited by NVME_CAP_MQES(cap) + 1 and the io_queue_depth module parameter (default 1024).
Test to provoke it
EXPERT: user-space driver creating a queue of MQES+2 entries.
S-33Abort Command Limit Exceeded (0x03) / 0x04 "Abort Command Is Missing" (reserved) ReportedNVMe admin
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: ACL+2 Abort SQEs without completions between them; the last one gets 0x103.
What happens
The host has more Abort commands outstanding than ACL+1 (Identify Controller ACL is 0's based). The extra Abort is rejected. 0x04 is listed by libnvme as "Abort command is missing". Linux names it NVME_SC_ABORT_MISSING but prints "Reserved" uncertain in current specs.
How it shows up
The Abort itself completes with 0x103. Linux logs "Abort status: 0x103" from pci.c:abort_endio().
Spec basis
Abort command (08h); ACL in Identify Controller (spec recommends at least 4, i.e. ACL ≥ 3).
Typical causes
Many simultaneous timeouts from a non-Linux host. Linux sets ctrl->abort_limit = id->acl + 1 and, in nvme_timeout(), does not send more aborts than that (it re-arms the timer instead). Linux therefore should not trigger this code unless ACL is reported wrongly.
How to detect / prove
Count outstanding Abort SQEs (opcode 08h) in the trace vs ACL from nvme id-ctrl.
Linux v7.2 source
pci.c:nvme_timeout() (atomic_dec_return(&dev->ctrl.abort_limit) < 0 → BLK_EH_RESET_TIMER).
Test to provoke it
EXPERT: user-space driver issuing ACL+2 aborts for commands stuck in a slow backend (QEMU).
S-34Asynchronous Event Request Limit Exceeded (SCT 1 / SC 0x05) ReportedNVMe admin / AEN
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: AER SQEs normally stay outstanding for hours. One that completes within microseconds with 0x105 is this error.
What happens
More AER commands are outstanding than the controller supports (Identify Controller AERL, 0's based). The extra AER completes at once with this status.
How it shows up
0x105 on an AER (opcode 0Ch). Linux's nvme_complete_async_event() returns early for any non-success AER status (if (le16_to_cpu(status) >> 1 != NVME_SC_SUCCESS) return;) and does not resubmit, so the error is not logged.
Spec basis
Asynchronous Event Request command; AERL (spec recommends at least 4 supported).
Typical causes
A host or tool submitting AERs in a loop; a controller with AERL=0 meeting a host that posts several. Linux posts only one (NVME_NR_AEN_COMMANDS = 1). QEMU: nvme_aer(): if (n->outstanding_aers > n->params.aerl) return NVME_AER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (no DNR).
How to detect / prove
Count outstanding opcode 0Ch commands in the trace; compare with AERL.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_complete_async_event(), pci.c:nvme_pci_submit_async_event() (fixed CID NVME_AQ_BLK_MQ_DEPTH).
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: -device nvme,aerl=0 plus a second AER sent with nvme admin-passthru --opcode=0x0c (it blocks until an event if accepted).
S-35Invalid Firmware Slot (SCT 1 / SC 0x06) ReportedNVMe admin / firmware
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Firmware Commit SQE CDW10[2:0] slot value → immediate CQE.
What happens
Firmware Commit named a slot that does not exist, or a read-only slot (slot 1 when FRMW.S1RO is set) for a replace action.
How it shows up
0x106 on Firmware Commit (opcode 10h). nvme-cli prints the status name.
Spec basis
Identify Controller FRMW: bit 0 slot 1 read-only, bits 3:1 number of slots, bit 4 activation without reset; Firmware Commit CDW10 FS (slot) and CA (commit action).
Typical causes
Update scripts written for a model with more slots; writing to slot 1 on drives where it holds the read-only factory image; slot 0 used with a CA that requires an explicit slot.
How to detect / prove
nvme id-ctrl -H /dev/nvme0 | grep -A5 frmw; nvme fw-log /dev/nvme0 shows populated slots.
Linux v7.2 source
The kernel does not issue Firmware Commit. Only passthrough (status returned raw to nvme-cli).
Test to provoke it
SAFE: nvme fw-commit /dev/nvme0 -s 7 -a 2 on a drive with fewer than 7 slots (CA 2 = activate existing image; no image is replaced).
S-36Invalid Firmware Image (0x07) and Overlapping Range (0x14) ReportedNVMe admin / firmware
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: A series of opcode 11h SQEs with OFST increasing by NUMD+1; a gap or overlap is visible directly.
What happens
0x07: the downloaded image failed validation (signature, CRC, wrong model, incomplete) at commit time. 0x14: Firmware Image Download pieces overlapped (the same offset range sent twice in an incompatible way).
How it shows up
0x107 on Firmware Commit, or 0x114 on Firmware Image Download/Commit. The running firmware is unchanged. Some drives also raise an Error AEN "Firmware Image Load Error" (05h) at a later activation.
Spec basis
Firmware Image Download (11h) NUMD/OFST in Dwords; FWUG (Firmware Update Granularity) in Identify Controller; Firmware Commit.
Typical causes
Wrong image file for the SKU; chunk size not a multiple of FWUG; tool retrying a chunk with a different offset; image signed for a different security version (anti-rollback).
How to detect / prove
Log every Firmware Image Download (offset, length) and check contiguity; compare nvme id-ctrl FWUG with the transfer size (nvme fw-download --xfer).
Linux v7.2 source
Passthrough only.
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: download a truncated or foreign image, then commit with CA=0 (replace, no activation). The drive must reject it without bricking. Run this as a robustness test.
S-37Invalid Interrupt Vector (SCT 1 / SC 0x08) ReportedNVMe admin / queues
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Create CQ CDW11[31:16] = vector ≥ table size.
What happens
Create I/O CQ named an interrupt vector the controller cannot use: beyond the MSI-X table size, or non-zero when MSI-X is disabled.
How it shows up
0x108; Linux continues with fewer queues.
Spec basis
Create I/O CQ CDW11 IV and IEN; PCIe MSI-X capability Table Size.
Typical causes
MSI-X table smaller than the advertised queue count; host fell back to MSI/INTx but still assigns per-queue vectors. QEMU nvme_create_cq(): if (!msix_enabled(...) && vector) and if (vector >= n->conf_msix_qsize).
How to detect / prove
lspci -vvv MSI-X "Count=" vs number of I/O queues; /proc/interrupts nvme entries.
Linux v7.2 source
pci.c:adapter_alloc_cq(); vector allocation in nvme_setup_irqs().
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: -device nvme,msix_qsize=2 with more queues requested; boot with pci=nomsi to see the non-MSI-X case.
S-38Invalid Log Page (SCT 1 / SC 0x09) ReportedNVMe admin / logs
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Get Log Page with CDW10[7:0]=LID → immediate CQE.
What happens
Get Log Page asked for an unsupported or reserved Log Identifier.
How it shows up
0x109. QEMU, however, returns Invalid Field (0x002) from nvme_get_log()'s default case. Implementations differ on which code they use impl.
Spec basis
Get Log Page (02h) LID; Supported Log Pages log (LID 00h, Linux NVME_LOG_SUPPORTED); LPA field in Identify Controller.
Typical causes
Tools asking for Persistent Event (0Dh), Telemetry (07h/08h) or vendor logs on drives without them.
How to detect / prove
nvme supported-log-pages /dev/nvme0 (if LID 00h is supported) and LPA bits in nvme id-ctrl -H.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_get_log(); the driver checks LPA before reading optional logs (e.g. command effects via NVME_CTRL_LPA_CMD_EFFECTS_LOG).
Test to provoke it
SAFE: nvme get-log /dev/nvme0 -i 0x30 -l 512.
S-39Invalid Format (SCT 1 / SC 0x0A) ReportedNVMe admin / format
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Format SQE (80h) → fast CQE. A real format takes seconds to hours.
What happens
Format NVM asked for an LBA format index that does not exist, or for a PI/metadata combination the namespace cannot support.
How it shows up
0x10A on Format NVM. The namespace is unchanged.
Spec basis
Identify Namespace NLBAF and LBAF[] table; Format NVM CDW10 LBAF, MSET, PI, PIL, SES.
Typical causes
LBAF index beyond NLBAF; PI type with a format whose metadata size is 0; extended LBA format index (above 15) without LBAFEE. QEMU: nvme_format_check() returns NVME_INVALID_FORMAT | NVME_DNR for lbaf > nlbaf and for PI on formats with metadata smaller than the PI size. nvme_copy() also uses it for formats it cannot copy between.
How to detect / prove
nvme id-ns -H /dev/nvme0n1 lists the LBA formats with "in use".
Linux v7.2 source
Passthrough only; Linux enables LBAFEE in Host Behavior Support when CTRATT.ELBAS is set (core.c:nvme_configure_host_options()).
Test to provoke it
SAFE (rejected before any erase): nvme format /dev/nvme0n1 -l 15 on a namespace with fewer formats.
S-40Firmware Activation Requires Reset: Conventional (0x0B), NVM Subsystem (0x10), Controller Level (0x11) ReportedNVMe admin / firmware
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Firmware Commit CQE with SCT 1 SC 0x0B/0x10/0x11; later CC.EN 1→0→1 (controller reset), PCIe hot/conventional reset, or a write of "NVMe" (4E564D65h) to NSSR.
What happens
These are successes reported as errors. The commit worked and the image is in the slot, but it will only run after the given type of reset. Until then the old firmware keeps running.
How it shows up
0x10B / 0x110 / 0x111 on Firmware Commit. Firmware Slot log (LID 03h) AFI: the "next active" slot (bits 6:4) differs from the current slot (bits 2:0). Linux reports this at AEN time as "Firmware is activated after next Controller Level Reset".
Spec basis
Firmware Commit CA values (libnvme: 0 replace, 1 replace+activate at reset, 2 activate at reset, 3 replace+activate immediately, 6/7 boot partition); Firmware Slot Information log AFI; NSSR register (20h) for subsystem reset.
Typical causes
Image needs a full reset to load; CA=1/2 used (activation at next reset by design). Scripts that treat any non-zero status as failure roll back a successful update. Scripts that ignore it think the new firmware is running when it is not.
How to detect / prove
nvme fw-log /dev/nvme0 AFI before and after; cat /sys/class/nvme/nvme0/firmware_rev stays old until reset; after a reset, check the revision again.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_get_fw_slot_info(): if (!cur_fw_slot || (next_fw_slot && (cur_fw_slot != next_fw_slot))) → "Firmware is activated after next Controller Level Reset"; reset via nvme reset /dev/nvme0 (NVME_IOCTL_RESET) or subsystem reset (NVME_IOCTL_SUBSYS_RESET, pci.c:nvme_pci_subsystem_reset()).
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: nvme fw-download a valid image, nvme fw-commit -s 2 -a 1, read status, then nvme reset /dev/nvme0 and verify firmware_rev. Use a supported vendor image only.
S-41Firmware Activation Requires Maximum Time Violation (0x12) / Activation Prohibited (0x13) ReportedNVMe admin / firmware
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Commit CDW10[5:3]=3 → CQE 0x12.
What happens
0x12: activating now (CA=3, immediate) would take longer than MTFA (Maximum Time for Firmware Activation, Identify Controller, 100 ms units), so the controller refuses. 0x13: the controller refuses this image for vendor-specific reasons (e.g. anti-rollback, a downgrade not allowed).
How it shows up
0x112 / 0x113 on Firmware Commit; the running firmware is unchanged.
Spec basis
MTFA; FRMW bit 4 (activation without reset supported); Firmware Commit CA=3.
Typical causes
Immediate activation of an image that changes the media layout; downgrade blocked by security policy.
How to detect / prove
Retry with CA=1/2 and a reset. If it works, the immediate path was the problem. For 0x13, check the vendor's release notes for minimum versions.
Linux v7.2 source
MTFA is stored in ctrl->mtfa and used by core.c:nvme_fw_act_work() to bound the wait while CSTS.PP is set after a "Firmware Activation Starting" AEN (S-81).
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: commit with CA=3 an image the vendor says needs a reset.
S-42Invalid Queue Deletion (SCT 1 / SC 0x0C) ReportedNVMe admin / queues
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: 04h before 00h.
What happens
Delete I/O CQ was sent for a CQ that still has SQs attached (they must be deleted first), or for the admin CQ.
How it shows up
0x10C on Delete I/O CQ (opcode 04h). QEMU returns it without DNR, so retrying after deleting the SQ is expected.
Spec basis
Delete I/O Completion Queue; queue deletion order (SQs before their CQ).
Typical causes
Teardown order bug in a host driver. QEMU nvme_del_cq(): if (!QTAILQ_EMPTY(&cq->sq_list)) return NVME_INVALID_QUEUE_DEL.
How to detect / prove
Trace order: Delete CQ (04h) issued before Delete SQ (00h) for an SQ mapped to that CQ.
Linux v7.2 source
pci.c:nvme_delete_io_queues() deletes SQs first, then CQs (passes of nvme_admin_delete_sq then nvme_admin_delete_cq).
Test to provoke it
EXPERT: user-space driver deleting the CQ first.
S-43Feature errors: Not Saveable (0x0D), Not Changeable (0x0E), Not Namespace Specific (0x0F) ReportedNVMe admin / features
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Set Features CDW10 bit 31 (SV) set → CQE 0x10D.
What happens
Set Features with SV=1 for a feature that cannot be saved (0x0D); a write to a read-only feature (0x0E); a namespace-specific NSID used with a controller-wide feature (0x0F).
How it shows up
0x10D/0x10E/0x10F with DNR=1 (QEMU). The current value is unchanged.
Spec basis
Set/Get Features, SV bit, Get Features SEL=11b "supported capabilities" (saveable, namespace-specific, changeable). ONCS bit "Save field in Set/Get Features".
Typical causes
Tools blindly setting --save. QEMU: nvme_set_feature() returns NVME_FID_NOT_SAVEABLE when save is set on any feature, NVME_FEAT_NOT_NS_SPEC for NSID ≠ 0/FFFFFFFFh on controller-scope features, NVME_FEAT_NOT_CHANGEABLE for fixed features.
How to detect / prove
nvme get-feature /dev/nvme0 -f <fid> -s 3 (capabilities) before setting.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_set_features() never sets SV. Errors come only from passthrough tools.
Test to provoke it
SAFE: nvme set-feature /dev/nvme0 -f 0x08 -v 0 --save (Interrupt Coalescing, saved) on a drive without saveable support.
S-44Namespace management/attachment errors: 0x15, 0x16, 0x18, 0x19, 0x1A, 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x24, 0x25 ReportedNVMe admin / namespaces
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Admin 0Dh/15h with a 4 KiB data buffer (namespace data or controller list) → CQE.
What happens
Namespace Management (0Dh) or Namespace Attachment (15h) refused: Namespace Insufficient Capacity (0x15), Namespace Identifier Unavailable (0x16, no free NSIDs), Namespace Already Attached (0x18), Namespace Is Private (0x19, already attached to another controller), Namespace Not Attached (0x1A, detach of a non-attached namespace), Thin Provisioning Not Supported (0x1B, NCAP < NSZE requested), Controller List Invalid (0x1C), ANA Group Identifier Invalid (0x24), ANA Attach Failed (0x25).
How it shows up
The matching 0x1xx status. Nothing changes.
Spec basis
Namespace Management create/delete; Namespace Attachment attach/detach with a Controller List; Identify TNVMCAP/UNVMCAP, NN, MNAN, ANAGRPMAX.
Typical causes
Provisioning scripts not checking UNVMCAP; wrong controller IDs (CNTLID) in the list; creating private namespaces on dual-port drives then attaching to both ports. QEMU nvme_ns_attachment() returns NS_ALREADY_ATTACHED, NS_PRIVATE, NS_NOT_ATTACHED, NS_CTRL_LIST_INVALID.
How to detect / prove
nvme id-ctrl (tnvmcap, unvmcap, nn, cntlid), nvme list-ctrl /dev/nvme0 -n <nsid>, nvme list-ns --all.
Linux v7.2 source
Passthrough only. After a successful change Linux rescans on the Namespace Attribute Changed AEN (core.c:nvme_handle_aen_notice() → nvme_queue_scan()).
Test to provoke it
CAUTION (the creates and deletes are destructive): on QEMU with -device nvme-subsys and nvme-ns,detached=true, attach the same namespace twice → 0x118.
S-45Device Self-test In Progress (SCT 1 / SC 0x1D) ReportedNVMe admin / self-test
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Two opcode 14h commands; the second gets 0x11D.
What happens
A Device Self-test (opcode 14h) was started while another self-test is running.
How it shows up
0x11D. Device Self-test log (LID 06h) byte 0 shows the current operation (1h short, 2h extended) and byte 1 the percent complete.
Spec basis
Device Self-test command STC (1h short, 2h extended, Fh abort); Device Self-test log; EDSTT (extended test time, minutes).
Typical causes
Monitoring agents (smartd, vendor tools) starting tests on a schedule while a manual test runs.
How to detect / prove
nvme self-test-log /dev/nvme0; abort with nvme device-self-test -s 0xf.
Linux v7.2 source
Passthrough only.
Test to provoke it
SAFE: nvme device-self-test /dev/nvme0 -s 2 twice in a row.
S-46Boot Partition Write Prohibited (SCT 1 / SC 0x1E) ReportedNVMe admin / boot partition
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Firmware Commit CA=6 → CQE 0x11E.
What happens
An attempt to change a locked Boot Partition (Firmware Image Download/Commit with boot-partition commit actions 6/7).
How it shows up
0x11E.
Spec basis
Boot Partitions (CAP.BPS, BPINFO/BPRSEL/BPMBL registers), Boot Partition Write Protection Config feature in newer revisions.
Typical causes
Platform locked the boot partition; tool writing the wrong partition.
How to detect / prove
nvme show-regs -H BPINFO; Boot Partition log (LID 15h).
Linux v7.2 source
Passthrough only.
Test to provoke it
EXPERT: platform with boot-partition lock.
S-47Virtualization management errors: 0x1F Invalid Controller Identifier, 0x20 Invalid Secondary Controller State, 0x21 Invalid Number of Controller Resources, 0x22 Invalid Resource Identifier ReportedNVMe admin / SR-IOV
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Admin 1Ch → CQE.
What happens
Virtualization Management (1Ch) refused: unknown secondary controller, secondary controller in the wrong state (online vs offline) for the action, resources (VQ/VI) over the flexible limit, or bad resource type.
How it shows up
0x11F–0x122 with DNR=1 (QEMU).
Spec basis
Virtualization Enhancements; Primary Controller Capabilities (CNS 14h), Secondary Controller List (CNS 15h).
Typical causes
Assigning resources to a VF that is online; asking for more queues than VQFRSM. QEMU: nvme_assign_virt_res_to_sec(), nvme_virt_set_state(), nvme_virt_mngmt().
How to detect / prove
nvme primary-ctrl-caps, nvme list-secondary.
Linux v7.2 source
Passthrough only.
Test to provoke it
SAFE on QEMU with sriov_max_vfs: assign resources to a secondary controller that is online.
S-48Sanitize Prohibited While Persistent Memory Region is Enabled (SCT 1 / SC 0x23) ReportedNVMe admin / sanitize
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Sanitize SQE → immediate CQE.
What happens
Sanitize was requested while the PMR is enabled (PMRCTL.EN=1).
How it shows up
0x123. Linux prints "Sanitize Prohibited".
Spec basis
Persistent Memory Region (CAP.PMRS, PMRCAP/PMRCTL registers); Sanitize.
Typical causes
Decommissioning scripts not disabling the PMR first.
How to detect / prove
nvme show-regs -H PMRCTL.
Linux v7.2 source
Passthrough only.
Test to provoke it
EXPERT: a PMR-capable controller (QEMU pmrdev=) with PMR enabled.

5.1 NVM command set specific (SCT 1, SC 0x80–0x8F)

S-49Conflicting Attributes (SCT 1 / SC 0x80) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: DSM (09h) SQE, MRd of the range list, CQE 0x180.
What happens
Dataset Management (or another NVM command) carries attribute bits that contradict each other or that the controller cannot honour together.
How it shows up
0x180 → Linux BLK_STS_NOTSUPP → -EOPNOTSUPP (a discard that fails this way looks like "discard not supported"). Persistent reservations map it to -EINVAL.
Spec basis
NVM Command Set: Dataset Management attributes (AD deallocate, IDR, IDW) and context attributes.
Typical causes
DSM with a combination the firmware does not implement; reservation commands with conflicting options.
How to detect / prove
Decode CDW11 of the DSM in the trace; repeat with only AD set.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status(); pr.c:nvme_status_to_pr_err().
Test to provoke it
SAFE via fault injection; on hardware, nvme dsm /dev/nvme0n1 -a 1 -d -w -r combinations (illustrative; check the nvme-cli syntax for your version).
S-50Invalid Protection Information (SCT 1 / SC 0x81) ReportedNVMe command / PI
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Immediate CQE, no data.
What happens
The PRINFO field (PRACT, PRCHK bits) is not valid for the namespace's PI type, or PI was requested on a namespace without PI.
How it shows up
0x181 → Linux BLK_STS_PROTECTION → -EILSEQ.
Spec basis
End-to-end Data Protection: Identify Namespace DPS/DPC, PRINFO in Read/Write/Compare/Verify CDW12.
Typical causes
Host sends PRCHK for Type 3 reference tag; PRACT with metadata size larger than the PI size in a mode the controller rejects. QEMU: nvme_do_write(), nvme_compare(), nvme_verify() return NVME_INVALID_PROT_INFO | NVME_DNR (e.g. Compare with PRACT set).
How to detect / prove
nvme id-ns -H DPS/DPC; decode CDW12[29:26] in the trace.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status(); PRINFO built in core.c:nvme_setup_rw() from the integrity profile.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU (PI namespace -device nvme-ns,pi=1,ms=8): nvme compare with PRACT set.
S-51Attempted Write to Read Only Range (SCT 1 / SC 0x82) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Write → CQE 0x182 (may follow data transfer).
What happens
A write touched an LBA range that the host previously marked read-only through the LBA Range Type feature (FID 03h).
How it shows up
0x182 → Linux BLK_STS_MEDIUM → -ENODATA ("critical medium error"). This is misleading: the media is fine and the cause is configuration.
Spec basis
LBA Range Type feature (attributes: read-only / hidden ranges). QEMU defines NVME_WRITE_TO_RO but never returns it.
Typical causes
OEM BIOS/firmware marked ranges read-only; old tools.
How to detect / prove
nvme get-feature /dev/nvme0 -n 1 -f 3 -H.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() (BLK_STS_MEDIUM).
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: set an LBA Range Type entry with the read-only attribute on a test drive that supports FID 03h.
S-52Command Size Limits Exceeded (0x83) and Copy-related 0x85/0x86/0x87/0x89 ReportedNVMe command / Copy
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Copy SQE → MRd of the source range descriptors → CQE.
What happens
A Copy (19h) or similar command exceeds MSSRL (max single source range length), MCL (max copy length) or MSRC (max source range count): 0x83. libnvme and QEMU add 0x85 Incompatible Namespace or Format, 0x86 Fast Copy Not Possible, 0x87 Overlapping I/O Range, 0x89 Insufficient Resources. These are not in Linux's nvme.h, so Linux prints them as "Unknown".
How it shows up
0x183 (Linux text "Command Size Limits Exceeded"); 0x185/0x187 from QEMU's nvme_do_copy().
Spec basis
NVM Command Set Copy command; Identify Namespace MSSRL/MCL/MSRC; ONCS Copy bit.
Typical causes
Copy offload with ranges built from filesystem extents larger than MSSRL; cross-namespace copy between different LBA formats (0x85); source overlapping destination (0x87). QEMU: nvme_check_copy_mcl(), nvme_copy().
How to detect / prove
nvme id-ns -H mssrl/mcl/msrc, then the Copy range list contents.
Linux v7.2 source
Default mapping (-EIO); Linux v7.2 does not issue Copy from the block layer in the paths examined here uncertain, so Copy errors come from passthrough.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: nvme copy with a range longer than MSSRL.
S-53Fabrics Connect/Discovery statuses: 0x80–0x84, 0x90 Discovery Restart, 0x91 Authentication Required ReportedNVMe-oF
In a PEX trace
Not visible Not on PCIe at all: NVMe-oF statuses travel in TCP/RDMA/FC response capsules, so a PEX capture of the NIC/HBA link shows only encrypted or opaque network DMA. Use a network capture (Wireshark NVMe/TCP dissector) or target logs. Pattern: Network capture: Fabrics command capsule (opcode 7Fh, fctype Connect) → response capsule with the status.
What happens
Fabrics Connect rejected: Incompatible Format (0x180), Controller Busy (0x181), Connect Invalid Parameters (0x182), Connect Restart Discovery (0x183), Connect Invalid Host (0x184). Also Discovery Restart (0x190) and Authentication Required (0x191). libnvme also lists 0x85 Invalid Queue Type for Disconnect.
How it shows up
Connect fails; nvme connect reports the error. dmesg from fabrics.c:nvmf_log_connect_error(). For 0x182 it decodes which parameter failed using the Connect response's IATTR/IPO fields. 0x191 on I/O → Linux disposition AUTHENTICATE → re-authentication work, then retry.
Spec basis
NVMe over Fabrics: Connect command and response, Discovery log, DH-HMAC-CHAP in-band authentication.
Typical causes
Host NQN not on the target's allow list (0x184); wrong subsystem NQN or CNTLID (0x182); dynamic controller already associated (0x181); keys not configured (0x191).
How to detect / prove
dmesg "Connect Invalid Host"/"Connect command failed ..." lines; target-side logs; nvme discover output.
Linux v7.2 source
fabrics.c:nvmf_log_connect_error(), nvmf_should_reconnect() path stops reconnecting when status & NVME_STATUS_DNR; core.c:nvme_decide_disposition() AUTHENTICATE branch. Note the string-table collision with NVM codes (§3.4.3).
Test to provoke it
SAFE: Linux nvmet loopback target without the host NQN in allowed_hosts → 0x184.

5.2 Zoned Namespace command set (SCT 1, SC 0xB6–0xBF)

ZNS errors are mostly the host breaking the zone state machine (write pointer, open and active limits). QEMU's ZNS model (nvme_check_zone_write(), nvme_check_zone_state_for_write(), nvme_zns_check_resources(), nvme_zrm_*()) returns all of them, so it is an excellent test device. Linux zoned users (f2fs, btrfs, dm-zoned, zonefs) get -EIO for most of them, but -EOVERFLOW / -ETOOMANYREFS for the active and open limits. libnvme also lists 0xB6 Invalid Zone Operation Request and 0xB7 ZRWA Resources Unavailable, which Linux's nvme.h lacks.

S-54Zone Boundary Error (SCT 1 / SC 0xB8) ReportedNVMe command / ZNS
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Write SQE near a zone end → CQE 0x1B8.
What happens
A command's LBA range spans more than one zone. For reads this is only an error if the namespace forbids cross-zone reads (Read Across Zone Boundaries, OZCS.RAZB=0).
How it shows up
0x1B8 → -EIO.
Spec basis
ZNS Command Set: zone size (ZSZE), OZCS RAZB.
Typical causes
Host splitting logic ignoring zone size (non-power-of-2 zone sizes are a classic trap). QEMU: nvme_check_zone_write(), nvme_check_zone_read().
How to detect / prove
nvme zns id-ns (zsze); compute slba / zsze and (slba+nlb-1) / zsze.
Linux v7.2 source
Block layer splits at chunk_sectors (zone size) so in-kernel I/O should not cross; default mapping in nvme_error_status().
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU ZNS: nvme read across a zone boundary.
S-55Zone Is Full (0xB9) / Zone Is Read Only (0xBA) / Zone Is Offline (0xBB) ReportedNVMe command / ZNS
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Write SQE → immediate CQE.
What happens
A write to a zone in ZSF:Full (0xB9) or ZSRO:Read Only (0xBA), or any access to a zone in ZSO:Offline (0xBB). Read Only and Offline are device-initiated states: the drive moved the zone there because of media problems. That makes them media-health events disguised as state errors.
How it shows up
0x1B9/0x1BA/0x1BB → -EIO. A zone report shows the zone state. The drive may also raise a Zone Descriptor Changed notice (ZNS-specific AEN) verify in spec.
Spec basis
ZNS zone states ZSE/ZSIO/ZSEO/ZSC/ZSF/ZSRO/ZSO; Zone Management Receive (report zones).
Typical causes
Host lost track of the write pointer after a crash (Full); worn or failed dies (Read Only, Offline). QEMU: nvme_check_zone_state_for_write(), nvme_check_zone_state_for_read().
How to detect / prove
nvme zns report-zones /dev/nvme0n1 -d 10; blkzone report; count zones in RO/Offline over time as a health metric.
Linux v7.2 source
zns.c (nvme_ns_report_zones()) converts zone states for the block layer; status → -EIO.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: fill a zone, then write again (0xB9). QEMU's Offline send action works only from Read Only (nvme_offline_zone()). Read Only and Offline must be entered by the device, so test 0xBA/0xBB with vendor injection or fault injection on the host.
S-56Zone Invalid Write (SCT 1 / SC 0xBC) ReportedNVMe command / ZNS
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Two Writes to the same zone completing out of order, or a re-submission after a host timeout.
What happens
A Write to a sequential-write-required zone did not start at the zone's write pointer.
How it shows up
0x1BC → -EIO. The most common ZNS error in the field.
Spec basis
ZNS sequential write requirement; Zone Append (opcode 7Dh) avoids it by letting the device choose the LBA.
Typical causes
Reordered writes (multiple queues, no zone write locking or plugging); retry of a write that actually succeeded (write pointer already advanced); host write-pointer cache stale after power loss. QEMU nvme_check_zone_write(): if (slba != zone->w_ptr) return NVME_ZONE_INVALID_WRITE.
How to detect / prove
Trace per-zone SLBA order and compare with the reported write pointer. A write that is reported failed but whose data is present means the earlier attempt succeeded.
Linux v7.2 source
Block layer zone write plugging keeps order. The NVMe driver maps the status to -EIO. Note the danger of nvme_decide_disposition() retries for zoned writes when DNR is clear derived.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: nvme write to zslba + 8 on an empty zone.
S-57Too Many Active Zones (0xBD) / Too Many Open Zones (0xBE) ReportedNVMe command / ZNS
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: A write to an empty zone → CQE 0x1BE.
What happens
Opening or writing a zone would exceed MAR (Maximum Active Resources) or MOR (Maximum Open Resources), both 0's based.
How it shows up
0x1BD → BLK_STS_ZONE_ACTIVE_RESOURCE → -EOVERFLOW; 0x1BE → BLK_STS_ZONE_OPEN_RESOURCE → -ETOOMANYREFS. These are the only zone codes with dedicated Linux errnos, so the filesystem can tell them apart and close zones.
Spec basis
ZNS Identify Namespace MAR/MOR; implicit vs explicit open.
Typical causes
Too many concurrent writers or log streams; not finishing zones. QEMU: nvme_zns_check_resources() (with DNR).
How to detect / prove
cat /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/max_open_zones and max_active_zones; count zones in open/closed states from a zone report.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status(); limits set in zns.c from MAR/MOR.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: -device nvme-ns,zoned=true,zoned.max_open=2, then write to 3 empty zones.
S-58Invalid Zone State Transition (0xBF) and Invalid Zone Operation Request (0xB6) / ZRWA Resources Unavailable (0xB7) ReportedNVMe command / ZNS
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Zone Management Send (79h) → CQE.
What happens
Zone Management Send asked for a transition the state machine does not allow (e.g. Open a Full zone, Finish an Offline zone) → 0xBF. 0xB6: invalid zone operation (e.g. allocating a ZRWA on a non-empty zone). 0xB7: no Zone Random Write Area available.
How it shows up
0x1BF → -EIO (Linux has no constant for 0xB6/0xB7 and prints "Unknown").
Spec basis
ZNS Zone Send Actions (Close, Finish, Open, Reset, Offline, Set Zone Descriptor Extension, Flush Explicit ZRWA Range).
Typical causes
Host state cache out of sync; tools sending Open to Full zones. QEMU: nvme_zrm_open_flags(), nvme_zrm_finish(), nvme_zrm_close(), nvme_zrm_reset(), nvme_offline_zone() return NVME_ZONE_INVAL_TRANSITION (no DNR); nvme_open_zone() returns NVME_INVALID_ZONE_OP / NVME_NOZRWA.
How to detect / prove
Zone report before the command; ZNS state diagram.
Linux v7.2 source
Zone ops (REQ_OP_ZONE_*) built in zns.c:nvme_setup_zone_mgmt_send().
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: nvme zns open-zone on a full zone.

6 Media and Data Integrity (SCT 2) and Path Related (SCT 3)

← 5 Command Specific Status (SCT 1)7 Complete Status Code Table →

SCT 2 codes are the ones operators fear. They mean the device could not store or return data correctly, or that a data-integrity check (Protection Information, Compare) failed. SCT 3 codes describe the route to the namespace, not the data. They exist so multipath hosts can pick another controller. Linux treats them very differently: most SCT 2 codes become -ENODATA ("critical medium error") or -EILSEQ, while on a multipath namespace every SCT 3 code triggers nvme_failover_req() and the application never sees it.

🌍 Analogy

An SCT 2 error is a library telling you "the book on that shelf is damaged". An SCT 3 error is "this branch can't reach that shelf right now, try the other branch". Retrying an SCT 2 read at the same library sometimes works, because the librarian tries harder. Retrying an SCT 3 error at the same branch rarely does.

Where the analogy breaks: a write fault is not like a damaged book. The library failed to shelve your book, and you may not know which copy, old or new, is now on the shelf.

6.1 Media and Data Integrity errors (SCT 2)

S-59Write Fault (SCT 2 / SC 0x80) ReportedNVMe command / media
In a PEX trace
Partly visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. The CQE and the full data transfer are visible; whether anything reached the media is not. Use read-back and SMART media_errors. Pattern: Write SQE → device MRd of all data (it was transferred) → after unusually long latency, CQE with SCT 2/SC 0x80.
What happens
The controller could not commit the write data to the media. The data was transferred from the host, but programming failed and the firmware could not place it elsewhere.
How it shows up
SCT 2 / SC 0x80 → Linux BLK_STS_MEDIUM → -ENODATA, dmesg "Write Fault" and "critical medium error ... op 0x1:(WRITE)". SMART "Media and Data Integrity Errors" increments. An Error Information log entry gives the LBA. Repeated faults usually come with Available Spare dropping and possibly critical warning bit 2 or 3 (S-74, S-75).
Spec basis
Media and Data Integrity Errors "Write Fault"; SMART/Health log Media and Data Integrity Errors counter; Error Information log LBA field.
Typical causes
Program failure with no spare blocks left; power-loss-protection capacitor failure making the drive refuse writes; drive entering read-only end-of-life mode in a vendor-specific way. QEMU: nvme_rw_complete_cb() maps any backend write error (Write, Write Zeroes, Zone Append) to NVME_WRITE_FAULT; nvme_flush_ns_cb() and nvme_copy_out_completed_cb() also return it.
How to detect / prove
nvme smart-log (media_errors, avail_spare, critical_warning); nvme error-log (LBA, NSID, status 0x280 in libnvme form is SCT 2/SC 0x80); read back the LBA. The old data, the new data or garbage can be returned. Record which.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() → BLK_STS_MEDIUM; filesystems usually go read-only on a failed metadata write.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU: attach the namespace through a blkdebug drive with an injected write error (event write_aio, errno 5) to get a real 0x280 CQE on the emulated wire. On hardware only vendor error injection works.
S-60Unrecovered Read Error (SCT 2 / SC 0x81) ReportedNVMe command / media
In a PEX trace
Partly visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. The CQE and the missing data MWrs are visible; the media cause is not (use the Error log LBA and SMART). Pattern: Read SQE → long latency (milliseconds instead of ~100 µs, from internal retries) → no data MWr, or partial → CQE SCT 2/0x81. With TLER set, the latency is capped.
What happens
The data could not be recovered from the media even after the controller's full error correction (ECC, read retries, soft decoding, RAID-like die parity). The data at those LBAs is lost unless the host has another copy.
How it shows up
SCT 2 / SC 0x81 on Read, Verify, Compare or Copy. Linux → BLK_STS_MEDIUM → -ENODATA. SMART media_errors increases. The Error Information log has the first failing LBA. Since the controller has already done its internal retries, DNR=1 is common. If DNR=0, Linux retries up to 5 times.
Spec basis
"Unrecovered Read Error"; Error Recovery feature (FID 05h) TLER (Time Limited Error Recovery) limits how long the drive tries before reporting; Write Uncorrectable (04h) marks LBAs to return this error on purpose.
Typical causes
Retention loss (data at rest too long, especially on hot drives), read disturb, worn blocks, firmware mapping bugs that point to the wrong physical page. Field data: Schroeder et al. (FAST '16) found that roughly 20–63% of drives in Google's fleet saw at least one uncorrectable error over four years, and that raw bit error rate was a poor predictor. QEMU: nvme_rw_complete_cb(), nvme_verify_cb(), nvme_compare_*_cb() map backend read errors to NVME_UNRECOVERED_READ.
How to detect / prove
Read the LBA range with nvme read and compare with nvme error-log. Use nvme verify (if ONCS supports it) to scan without moving data. Rewrite the LBA (that usually remaps it), then re-read to confirm.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status(); nvme_log_error() prints "@ LBA x, n blocks" for the whole request (not the exact bad LBA).
Test to provoke it
CAUTION (destroys data in the range): nvme write-uncor /dev/nvme0n1 -s 0x1000 -c 7, then nvme read ... -s 0x1000 → 0x281. Then nvme write-zeroes or a normal write clears it. In QEMU, use blkdebug read_aio errors.
S-61End-to-end PI check errors: Guard (0x82), Application Tag (0x83), Reference Tag (0x84), Storage Tag (0x88) ReportedNVMe command / PI
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. If the metadata crosses the link (separate MPTR buffer or extended LBA), the PI tuple is in the payload and the guard can be recomputed offline from the trace. Pattern: Read with PRINFO bits in CDW12 → data and metadata MWr (on read checks the data is often transferred first) → CQE 0x82–0x84.
What happens
On a namespace formatted with Protection Information, a check enabled by PRCHK failed. Guard: CRC of the data does not match the guard field, so the data or metadata was corrupted. App Tag: the tag differs from the expected value (under the mask). Ref Tag: the block is not the LBA the host expected, for example a misdirected write or read. Storage Tag (0x88, libnvme/QEMU only; Linux nvme.h has no constant): the storage tag check failed.
How it shows up
0x282/0x283/0x284 → Linux BLK_STS_PROTECTION → -EILSEQ ("protection error"). 0x288 → "Unknown" → -EIO. The checks can run on writes (PRACT=0, the controller verifies host-supplied PI) or on reads.
Spec basis
End-to-end Data Protection (Type 1/2/3; 16-bit guard CRC-16 T10-DIF, and 32/64-bit guard formats in newer revisions); PRINFO = PRACT + PRCHK[2:0]; ELBAT/ELBATM/ILBRT fields.
Typical causes
Guard: DMA corruption, controller SRAM/DRAM bit flips, wrong PI generation by the host (bad CRC table, wrong byte order). Ref: host reused a buffer from a different LBA, firmware L2P mapping bug (misdirected write), Type 1 reference tag not incremented across blocks. App: application-tag misuse. QEMU dif.c:nvme_dif_prchk_crc16() shows the exact algorithm and the escape values. For Type 1/2 an app tag of FFFFh disables checking. For Type 3 the app tag FFFFh and ref tag FFFFFFFFh are needed.
How to detect / prove
Read the block with PRCHK cleared plus its metadata (nvme read ... -y 8 -M meta.bin), recompute CRC-16 T10-DIF over the data and compare the stored guard; the stored ref tag shows which LBA's data you got. This is one of the few ways to prove a misdirected write.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() → BLK_STS_PROTECTION; PRINFO and reftag setup in core.c:nvme_setup_rw(); module parameter disable_pi_offsets in core.c changes how PI offsets are handled.
Test to provoke it
SAFE in QEMU (-device nvme-ns,ms=8,pi=1): write with correct PI, then read with PRCHK=ref and a wrong ILBRT (nvme read ... -p 1 -r 0x1234) → 0x284. Write data with a bad guard → 0x282.
S-62Compare Failure (SCT 2 / SC 0x85) ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Compare SQE → device MRd of the host buffer → CQE 0x285.
What happens
A Compare (05h) found that the media data differs from the host buffer. This is an expected result, not a fault, for compare-and-write locking. As the first half of a fused pair it also aborts the second half (0x09).
How it shows up
0x285 → Linux BLK_STS_MEDIUM → -ENODATA, so it looks like a medium error in dmesg. Monitoring tools that count "critical medium error" lines over-count on systems using Compare (e.g. VMware-style ATS-like locking over NVMe-oF).
Spec basis
NVM Compare command; Fused Operation; ONCS Compare bit.
Typical causes
Lock contention (expected); stale data after a lost write (unexpected and worth investigating). QEMU: nvme_compare_data_cb(), nvme_compare_mdata_cb() (data and metadata compared separately).
How to detect / prove
Read the LBA and diff it against the compare buffer; check whether the differing data matches an older write (lost-write detection).
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() (BLK_STS_MEDIUM). Compare is not issued by the block layer; it comes from passthrough or targets.
Test to provoke it
SAFE: nvme compare /dev/nvme0n1 -s 0 -c 0 -z 4096 -d /dev/urandom (random data will not match).
S-63Access Denied (SCT 2 / SC 0x86) ReportedNVMe command / security
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: Reads → immediate CQE 0x286 (no media latency).
What happens
Access to the namespace or LBA range is denied because of missing access rights, typically a locked range of a self-encrypting drive.
How it shows up
0x286 → Linux BLK_STS_MEDIUM → -ENODATA. On boot this looks like a dying disk ("critical medium error" on every read of the partition table) when the drive is simply locked.
Spec basis
Media and Data Integrity "Access Denied"; TCG Storage Opal/Enterprise locking ranges via Security Send/Receive.
Typical causes
Opal locking range locked after power cycle; S3 resume without re-unlock (Linux supports Opal unlock on resume through sed-opal).
How to detect / prove
sedutil-cli --query /dev/nvme0 shows Locked = Y; all failing LBAs fall inside one locking range.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status(); Opal through core.c:nvme_sec_submit() and block/sed-opal.c.
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: lock a range on a test SED and read it. Keep the admin password safe.
S-64Deallocated or Unwritten Logical Block (SCT 2 / SC 0x87) — DULBE ReportedNVMe command
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. This is one of the few ways a PEX trace can prove a deallocation took effect: with DULBE enabled, a read of the trimmed range returns SC 0x87 and no data MWr. Pattern: Read SQE → immediate CQE 0x287, no data.
What happens
A Read, Verify, Compare or Copy touched a deallocated or never-written LBA, and the host enabled DULBE (Deallocated or Unwritten Logical Block Error) in the Error Recovery feature. Without DULBE the drive returns the deallocated read pattern (often zeros; see DLFEAT) with success.
How it shows up
0x287 → Linux BLK_STS_MEDIUM → -ENODATA. It is a useful error. It is also the only way, other than LBA Status, to prove that a Deallocate actually took effect: after deallocating a range, reads with DULBE on must fail with 0x287.
Spec basis
Error Recovery feature (FID 05h) DULBE bit; Identify Namespace NSFEAT DAE bit (DULBE supported); DLFEAT (read behaviour of deallocated blocks).
Typical causes
Host enabled DULBE and then reads unwritten space (partition probing, filesystem scans). Linux never sets DULBE because it would break partition and filesystem probing (Christoph Hellwig, linux-nvme 2018). Arrays sometimes return it even when DULBE is off, which is a vendor bug (Hannes Reinecke in the same thread). QEMU: nvme_check_dulbe() uses the backend's block status (unallocated → NVME_DULB) when NVME_ERR_REC_DULBE(ns->features.err_rec) is set.
How to detect / prove
nvme get-feature /dev/nvme0 -n 1 -f 5 shows whether DULBE is on. As a deallocation proof: write a pattern, nvme dsm -d the range, enable DULBE, read → expect 0x287. If the read returns the old pattern with success, the deallocation was silently ignored.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_error_status() (UNWRITTEN_BLOCK → BLK_STS_MEDIUM).
Test to provoke it
CAUTION (the DSM step destroys data): on a scratch namespace, nvme set-feature /dev/nvme0 -n 1 -f 5 -v 0x10000 (DULBE is bit 16 of the Error Recovery value), deallocate a range, read it, then set the feature back to its previous value.

6.2 Path Related Status (SCT 3)

The ANA codes 0x01–0x03 carry the Asymmetric Namespace Access state of the controller–namespace relationship. 0x00 is a controller-internal path error. 0x60 is a controller-detected pathing error, and 0x70/0x71 are host-detected. Linux's nvme_is_path_error() checks only (status & NVME_SCT_MASK) == NVME_SCT_PATH, so every SCT 3 code fails over on a multipath head. nvme_is_ana_error() additionally schedules an ANA log re-read for 0x301–0x303.

S-65Internal Path Error (SCT 3 / SC 0x00) ReportedNVMe command / path
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: On path A: CQE 0x300; the same LBA then appears on path B.
What happens
The command failed because of an internal error specific to the controller processing it, so another controller (path) to the same namespace may succeed (libnvme wording).
How it shows up
0x300. Multipath: failover, multipath_failover_count increases, and the I/O succeeds on the other path. Single path: retry, then -EIO.
Spec basis
Path Related Status "Internal Path Error".
Typical causes
One controller of a dual-controller array failing its back-end link; one port of a dual-port SSD with an internal fault.
How to detect / prove
nvme list-subsys path states; failover counters per path; correlate with array logs.
Linux v7.2 source
nvme.h:nvme_is_path_error(), multipath.c:nvme_failover_req() (nvme_mpath_clear_current_path(), requeue on the head).
Test to provoke it
SAFE: fault-inject 0x300 on one path's namespace device (the hidden nvme0c0n1-style node) and watch I/O continue.
S-66ANA path errors: Persistent Loss (0x01), Inaccessible (0x02), Transition (0x03) ReportedNVMe command / ANA multipath
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: CQEs with SCT 3 on one controller; Get Log Page LID 0Ch shortly after; I/O moves to the other controller.
What happens
The namespace's ANA group on this controller is in Inaccessible (0x02), Persistent Loss (0x01) or Change/Transition (0x03) state, so the command cannot be served on this path.
How it shows up
0x301/0x302/0x303. Linux multipath: nvme_failover_req() sets NVME_NS_ANA_PENDING and queues ana_work to re-read the ANA log (LID 0Ch), then resubmits the bios on another path. Usually an ANA Change AEN (S-83) arrives too. Without multipath (nvme_core.multipath=N), the code is retried on the same path and ends in -EIO.
Spec basis
Asymmetric Namespace Access: ANA log page (groups, states Optimized 01h, Non-Optimized 02h, Inaccessible 03h, Persistent Loss 04h, Change 0Fh — Linux enum nvme_ana_state), ANATT (ANA Transition Time, seconds), ANACAP, ANAGRPID.
Typical causes
Array controller failover or firmware upgrade (Transition); a path to a namespace owned by the peer controller (Inaccessible); controller permanently lost access (Persistent Loss).
How to detect / prove
nvme ana-log /dev/nvme0; cat /sys/block/nvme0c0n1/ana_state; failover counters; dmesg "ANATT timeout, resetting controller." if a transition outlasts ANATT.
Linux v7.2 source
multipath.c:nvme_failover_req(), nvme_update_ana_state(), nvme_anatt_timeout() (resets the controller after ANATT×2 seconds of Change state, via mod_timer(&ctrl->anatt_timer, ctrl->anatt * HZ * 2 + jiffies)); nvme.h:nvme_is_ana_error().
Test to provoke it
SAFE: Linux nvmet target with two ports; change a port's ANA state through configfs (ana_groups/<id>/ana_state) to "inaccessible" or "change" and run fio on the host.
S-67Controller Pathing Error (SCT 3 / SC 0x60) ReportedNVMe-oF / path
In a PEX trace
Partly visible On NVMe/PCIe the CQE with SCT 3/SC 0x60 is visible like any other; on fabrics (the usual case) it is not on PCIe. Pattern: Response capsule with SCT 3/SC 0x60.
What happens
The controller detected a pathing error, e.g. a fabrics transport problem between itself and the host, or within the subsystem.
How it shows up
0x360 → failover on multipath; default -EIO otherwise.
Spec basis
Path Related Status "Controller Pathing Error" (controller-detected range 60h–6Fh).
Typical causes
Target-side transport errors; fabric port reset.
How to detect / prove
Target logs; failover counters; network counters on the target side.
Linux v7.2 source
Same path as S-65.
Test to provoke it
SAFE via fault injection 0x360.
S-68Host Pathing Error (SCT 3 / SC 0x70) — host-generated ReportedHost driver / path
In a PEX trace
Not visible Host-generated: no CQE carries 0x370. At most you see that the command was never submitted (no SQ doorbell MWr) while the controller was being reset. Evidence: the nvme:nvme_complete_rq tracepoint and dmesg. Pattern: Nothing. The command was never submitted, or was submitted to a dead link.
What happens
The host detected that it cannot reach the controller. Linux sets this status itself when a request cannot be queued to a controller that is not live (e.g. during reconnect).
How it shows up
No CQE on the wire. Linux: status 0x370 → FAILOVER on multipath, otherwise BLK_STS_TRANSPORT → -ENOLINK ("recoverable transport error").
Spec basis
Path Related Status "Host Pathing Error" (host-detected range 70h–7Fh).
Typical causes
Fabrics connection lost; PCIe controller in RESETTING/DELETING; the driver's nvme_fail_nonready_command() path for non-ready controllers.
How to detect / prove
dmesg controller state changes ("resetting controller", reconnect attempts) right before; tracepoint status 0x370 with no matching CQE in an analyzer capture.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_host_path_error(), core.c:nvme_fail_nonready_command(), core.c:nvme_error_status() → BLK_STS_TRANSPORT.
Test to provoke it
SAFE: NVMe/TCP loopback, take the target port down (ip link set ... down) with fast_io_fail_tmo set, run I/O.
S-69Host Aborted Command (SCT 3 / SC 0x71) — host-generated ReportedHost driver
In a PEX trace
Partly visible 0x371 itself is never on the wire (host-generated). What is visible is the cause and the reset: outstanding SQEs with no CQE, then CC.EN←0 (MWr to BAR0+14h) and re-initialisation. Pattern: No CQE with 0x371. You see the reset itself: CC.EN←0 (MWr to offset 14h), CSTS.RDY→0, re-enable.
What happens
The host cancelled the command because of a host action. Linux sets it on every in-flight request when it tears down a controller's queues (reset after timeout or CSTS.CFS, removal, transport error recovery).
How it shows up
dmesg nvme_log_error lines with "Host Aborted Command (sct 0x3 / sc 0x71)" for many requests at once, usually right after "I/O tag N ... timeout, reset controller" or "controller is down; will reset". Being SCT 3 it fails over on multipath; otherwise it is retried after the reset, or -EIO if the controller is removed.
Spec basis
Path Related Status "Command Aborted By Host" (libnvme NVME_SC_CMD_ABORTED_BY_HOST).
Typical causes
It is always a symptom. The cause is earlier: a command timeout, a fatal controller status, a PCIe error (AER/DPC), or surprise removal.
How to detect / prove
Read dmesg backwards from the first 0x371 to the first timeout, CFS or AER message. In an analyzer capture, find the last good CQE and what the device stopped doing.
Linux v7.2 source
core.c:nvme_cancel_request() (nvme_req(req)->status = NVME_SC_HOST_ABORTED_CMD), nvme_cancel_tagset(), nvme_cancel_admin_tagset().
Test to provoke it
CAUTION: nvme reset /dev/nvme0 during heavy fio; or echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/<bdf>/remove (EXPERT: device disappears until rescan).
S-70Vendor Specific status (SCT 7) and reserved SCT 4–6 ReportedNVMe command / vendor
In a PEX trace
Visible The status is in DW3 of the 16-byte CQE that the device writes with a device→host MWr to the CQ base address + head×16; the analyzer's NVMe decoder pairs it with the SQE by SQID/CID. Pattern: CQE DW3 bits 27:25 = 111b.
What happens
The controller reports a vendor-defined status (SCT 7). SCT 4–6 are reserved, and receiving one is a device bug.
How it shows up
Linux prints "Unknown (sct 0x7 / sc 0x..)" and maps it to BLK_STS_IOERR → -EIO; retried unless DNR.
Spec basis
Status Code Type 7h = Vendor Specific (libnvme NVME_SCT_VS).
Typical causes
Vendor commands; firmware debug builds; drives that use SCT 7 for internal faults that should have used Internal Error.
How to detect / prove
Ask the vendor for the code table; capture telemetry right after.
Linux v7.2 source
constants.c:nvme_get_error_status_str() → "Unknown".
Test to provoke it
SAFE via fault injection status 0x7xx.
Synthetic trace — ANA transition on a two-controller array with Linux native multipath
#t (ms)PathEventDetail
10ctrl AWrite CID 0x0012ANA group 1 Optimized on A
23ctrl ACQE SCT 3 / SC 0x03ANA Transition; DNR=0
33hostnvme_failover_req()NVME_NS_ANA_PENDING set, ana_work queued, bio requeued on head
43ctrl AAER completionNotice / ANA Change (subtype 03h), log page 0Ch
54ctrl BWrite (same LBA)group 1 Non-Optimized on B; succeeds
65ctrl AGet Log Page LID 0Chgroup 1: Change (0Fh) → timer armed (ANATT×2)
72100ctrl AAER + ANA loggroup 1 Optimized on A again; I/O returns to A

The application saw no error. The only evidence is multipath_failover_count, the nvme:nvme_async_event tracepoint and a latency spike. If step 7 never came, Linux would reset controller A after 2×ANATT seconds ("ANATT timeout, resetting controller.").

7 Complete Status Code Table

← 6 Media and Data Integrity (SCT 2) and Path Related (SCT 3)III.1 Time Is an Error Signal →

Every status code defined in Linux v7.2 include/linux/nvme.h appears below, in Linux's shifted layout (SCT in bits 10:8, SC in bits 7:0). The "Linux string" column is what nvme_get_error_status_str() prints. The errno column follows nvme_error_status() plus blk_errors[]. A dash means the code only occurs on admin/passthrough commands, where nvme-cli gets the raw status and no errno mapping applies. "Retry? (typical)" is what the code usually means for a retry, based on the spec wording and QEMU's DNR use derived. The authoritative signal is always the DNR bit in the actual CQE, and Linux retries anything without DNR (§3.4.1). The PEX column says whether the status itself can be read from a PCIe analyzer capture of the SSD link: "Visible" means the CQE is a device→host MWr whose payload holds the status.

7.1 Generic Command Status (SCT 0)

Linux valueSCT / SCLinux constant (card)Linux string (constants.c)MeaningRetry? (typical)Linux errnoTypical causePEX trace
